title: They said a man teaches him, a man who barely spoke Arabic.
subtitle: An accusation that falls apart on its own
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators pointed to {trap}a non-Arab servant who sold goods by As-Safa{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ may have sat and talked with him a little, but the man knew only simple Arabic phrases. {idea}How could the Quran, with its eloquent style and perfect meanings, come from him?{/idea}
now: When you want to dismiss something, you grab any explanation, even one that makes no sense. A colleague's success? Must be connections. {trap}A rushed accusation often says more about us than them.{/trap}
old: If I can find any explanation, I don't have to accept it.
new: An explanation that makes no sense is just a way to avoid the truth.
try: Before you dismiss something today, ask if your reason would convince a fair person.

title: Those who refuse His signs are left without guidance.
subtitle: Guidance needs a heart that wants it
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah does not guide {trap}those who turn away from remembering Him, who are heedless, and who have no intention of believing.{/trap} Such people will not be guided by the signs, because they never wanted to be.
now: You say you want to change, but you avoid every talk, every reminder, every friend who might push you. {idea}Guidance comes to those who want it.{/idea} Wanting it starts with not running from it.
old: If Allah wanted me guided, it would just happen.
new: Guidance meets those who turn toward it; refusing it closes the door.
try: Make a sincere dua today: O Allah, make me want what You want for me.

title: The liars are the ones who invent lies, not Al-Amin.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ was known for honesty
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ {reward}was known among his people for his truthfulness; they called him Al-Amin.{/reward} When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan if they ever accused him of lying before his claim, Abu Sufyan said no. Heraclius reasoned: {idea}would he refrain from lying about people, then lie about Allah?{/idea}
now: Your record is your witness. The coworker who never fudges a timesheet is believed when it matters. {reward}Small daily honesty builds the trust that speaks for you later.{/reward}
old: Little lies don't affect my credibility.
new: A track record of honesty is what makes people trust my word.
try: Go a full day without a single exaggeration or white lie.

title: Forced words with a heart at peace in faith are excused.
subtitle: The heart decides, not words under torture
then: Persecution in Makkah was at its height when this came. Ibn Kathir describes the one who {idea}says words of disbelief under beatings and abuse while his heart refuses them.{/idea} He mentions Bilal, who under {trap}a huge rock on his chest in the heat{/trap} kept saying: Alone, Alone.
now: You may never face torture, but you face pressure: the joke you laugh along with to fit in, the silence when your faith is mocked. {idea}Your heart knows the difference between being cornered and choosing.{/idea} {reward}Bilal's courage is a light for smaller tests.{/reward}
old: Only my words show what I believe.
new: Allah sees the heart; and steadfastness under pressure is precious.
try: Next time your faith is mocked in a small way, say one calm, kind word for it.

title: They preferred this world over the Hereafter.
subtitle: The root reason for leaving faith
then: Ibn Kathir says these people {trap}understood the faith yet still turned away from it{/trap}, because they preferred this life to the Hereafter. They {trap}left the faith for the sake of this world.{/trap}
now: A job offer that requires you to drop your prayers. A relationship that pulls you away from Allah. {idea}The trade is rarely presented as leaving faith. It is presented as a good deal.{/idea}
old: I can always balance this world and my faith later.
new: When I put this world above the next, I start to drift from faith.
try: Look at one big decision you're weighing and ask: what does it cost my akhirah?

title: Hearts, ears and eyes sealed: they became the heedless.
subtitle: Senses that no longer help
then: Earlier in the surah, hearing, sight and hearts were listed as gifts for gratitude. Ibn Kathir says here Allah {trap}put a seal on their hearts so they would not understand what benefits them{/trap}, and sealed their ears and eyes. {trap}Their faculties did not help them at all.{/trap}
now: You hear the Quran in the car and it doesn't land. You watch a funeral pass and feel nothing. {idea}Numbness is a warning sign, not a resting place.{/idea} {reward}A heart can be softened while it still beats.{/reward}
old: Feeling nothing at reminders is just how I am.
new: A heart that stops responding needs care before it hardens further.
try: Sit with one verse of the Quran today until something in it moves you.

title: No doubt, in the Hereafter they are the losers.
subtitle: The final result of choosing this world
then: Ibn Kathir says la jarama means it is inevitable that those who are like this {trap}will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.{/trap} This closes the passage about those who traded faith for the world.
now: You track wins: the promotion, the new car, the followers. {idea}Picture the final scoreboard, where only one column counts.{/idea} Losing yourself is the only loss that cannot be recovered.
old: As long as I'm winning here, I'm doing fine.
new: The real loss is losing myself in the Hereafter, whatever I gain here.
try: Write one line tonight: what am I building that will still count on that Day?

title: They gave in under trial, then emigrated and endured. He forgives.
subtitle: A way back for those who once broke
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to people {trap}oppressed in Makkah, whose position was weak, who went along with their people when tried.{/trap} Then they escaped, leaving homeland, families and wealth, joined the believers and bore hardship with patience. {reward}Allah tells them He will forgive and show mercy.{/reward}
now: You gave in once, badly. Maybe you left prayer for years, or did something you can't say out loud. {reward}This verse is for people who fell and then got up and kept going.{/reward} What you do after counts.
old: Once I've failed that badly, there's no way back.
new: Allah forgives those who fall, then turn, strive and stay patient.
try: Take one concrete step back toward Allah today from a place where you once fell.

title: Every soul comes pleading for itself, and no one is wronged.
subtitle: Alone with your record, and full justice
then: Ibn Kathir says each person will make a case in his own defense, {trap}no one else will plead for him: not father, son, brother or wife.{/trap} Each will be paid for what he did, good or evil, {idea}with no decrease in reward and no increase in punishment.{/idea}
now: You rely on being part of a good family, a good mosque, a good group. On that Day you'll stand on your own. {reward}Every quiet good deed you did will be there, none missing.{/reward}
old: My family and community will carry me through.
new: I will stand for myself, and every good I did will be counted exactly.
try: Do one good deed today that no one else will ever know about.

title: A safe, well-fed town denied His favors and tasted hunger and fear.
subtitle: The example of Makkah
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the example of Makkah, {reward}a secure sanctuary while people outside were being snatched away.{/reward} They denied Allah's favors, the greatest being the Prophet ﷺ sent to them. When they insisted on opposing him, {trap}they were struck with years of famine{/trap}, and their security turned to fear.
now: Your city is safe, your shops are full, the lights always come on. It's easy to forget that these are favors. {idea}Gratitude is how you hold on to what you have.{/idea}
old: Safety and plenty are just normal.
new: Safety and plenty are favors that need gratitude to last.
try: Thank Allah today, by name, for the safety of your home and the food in your kitchen.

title: A Messenger came from among them, and they denied him.
subtitle: The greatest favor, rejected
then: Ibn Kathir says this happened because of {trap}their rejection of the Messenger ﷺ that Allah sent to them from among themselves.{/trap} He reminds of the verses calling this a blessing: a Messenger {reward}reciting His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.{/reward}
now: You have the Sunnah at your fingertips: his words, his manners, his prayers, all a search away. {idea}A favor ignored is a favor slowly lost.{/idea}
old: The Prophet's ﷺ example is nice but not urgent for me.
new: The Prophet ﷺ is one of the greatest favors given to me.
try: Learn one sunnah today and practice it before the day ends.

title: Eat what is lawful and good, and be grateful.
subtitle: After famine, an invitation to eat and thank
then: Right after the example of the town that tasted famine, the verse turns to believers. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}orders His believing servants to eat the good and lawful things He provided and to give thanks{/idea}, for He is the Giver of all favors and alone deserves worship.
now: Lunch at your desk, eaten while scrolling, barely tasted. {idea}The same meal eaten with bismillah and alhamdulillah becomes worship.{/idea}
new: Eating good and lawful food with thanks is a way of worshipping Allah.
try: Eat one meal today without your phone, starting with bismillah and ending with alhamdulillah.

title: Only a few things are forbidden, and need finds mercy.
subtitle: A short list and a wide door
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah mentions what He forbade, {trap}things which harm people in both religious and worldly affairs.{/trap} Yet if someone is forced by need, without deliberately disobeying, {reward}Allah is Pardoning, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: Sometimes faith feels like a long list of no. Read the verse again: {idea}a handful of limits on one side, a whole world of good food on the other.{/idea} And mercy for real need.
old: Religion is mostly about what I can't have.
new: Allah made the good wide and the forbidden few, with mercy for need.
try: Name five good foods you enjoy, and thank Allah for each.
